items.context: @cryptogoos (121.023 seguidores, en inglés): 'la historia se repite: compra $BTC 500 días antes del halving, vende 500 días después, repite', con video. Post de ~20 minutos, 3.334 vistas, 34 likes, 5 guardados y solo 4 respuestas: tema halving, respondible con el post de emisión (3,125% restante, subsidio de 3,125 a 1,5625 BTC por bloque).
items.suggested_text:
The rhythm has held so far, but the engine behind it gets weaker every cycle. A halving works by cutting new supply that miners have to sell. At the next one, the subsidy drops from 3.125 to 1.5625 BTC per block, roughly from ~450 to ~225 BTC a day, and only 3.125% of the 21M will be left to issue.

In 2012, halving the subsidy was a real shock to the float. Today, a single week of ETF flows can move more coins than miners produce in months. So the calendar can keep working for a different reason: not because supply gets scarcer, but because millions of people now trade the expectation itself.

A pattern that survives because everyone believes in it is a different animal from one that survives because of supply.
